issue_context.title: Pessimistic DML should not lock non-unique index keys
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
create table t(id varchar(40), v int, PRIMARY KEY (`id`) clustered, key i2(v))
insert into t values ('123', 1)
begin pessimistic
update t set v = v + 1 where id = '123'
commit
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

The update statement is not supposed to lock the index key.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

The update statement acquires a pessimistic lock for the index key.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

master (987bdd3014d8c90302caac3e99092d8014c47109)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
comments:
@ekexium

After this for such execution plans:
```
update uk = uk where sk = 1; // The uk value is not changed
The plan:
update
    select lock
        index look up 
```
The unique key could be locked but https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/25730 would not work so the LOCK record could accumulate and lead to performance issues.

/cc @you06 @MyonKeminta @sticnarf

review_comments: So, we don't need to consider the untouched flag here?

Why the old code fail to work?
For unique index, the value is encoded in the kv key part, so kv value part is not set.
For non-unique index, the value is encoded in the kv value part.
Can't `len(v) == 1` distinguish them?

OK, get it.
In a previous refactoring, the [key-value encoding format](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Co5iMiaxitv3okJmLYLJxZYCNChcjzswJMRr-_45Eqg/edit#heading=h.l238zyi79ds4) is changed

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1420062/180726185-0cd89774-be49-43e9-bdcf-8fe3d28548b9.png)
In which version we changed key-value encoding format ?
Since the introducing of global index / clustered index / collation, whichever comes first. @TonsnakeLin
